question_text: Analysis of a nickel casting suggests that $28 \%$ of the solidification process occurred in a dendritic manner. Calculate the temperature at which nucleation occurred. The specific heat of nickel is $4.1 \mathrm{~J} /\left(\mathrm{cm}^3 \cdot{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$. Give your answer as the value of nucleation_temperature.The unit of the answer is °C.
response:
Using standard nickel properties:
- Melting point: $T_m = 1455\,°\text{C}$
- Latent heat of fusion: $L = 17.2\,\text{kJ/mol}$, with $\rho = 8.902\,\text{g/cm}^3$ and $M = 58.69\,\text{g/mol}$, giving $L = 2608.9\,\text{J/cm}^3$

$$\Delta T = \frac{0.28 \times 2608.9}{4.1} = 178.2\,°\text{C}$$

$$T_n = 1455 - 178.2 = 1276.8\,°\text{C} \approx 1277\,°\text{C}$$

$$\boxed{1277}$$
